A1.justification: Both complete, readable 14-page PDFs describe the same FUSER/FUSER-DF work, including Appendices A–D. Pages 2–13 are textually and visually identical; differences are confined to the first-page version/date stamp and Appendix Figure 7.

before.justification: v2 reports original registration experiments on ScanNet, 3DMatch, and ArkitScenes, ablations and efficiency measurements in Tables 1–5, and real-world iPhone case studies in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results and case studies, with revised runtime figures and newly reported GPU-memory measurements in Figure 7.

M1.justification: The FUSER encoder, alternating attention, pose prediction and losses, and FUSER-DF diffusion procedure are unchanged. Section 3 and Appendix C retain identical method descriptions and architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training and evaluation datasets and the same kitchen/living-room and study-room iPhone scenarios. Figure 7 displays additional input thumbnails without establishing new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–3 and the qualitative comparisons is identical. Figure 7 remains a demonstration of FUSER without competing methods.

E3.justification: The main benchmark protocols and Appendix A metrics are unchanged. However, Figure 7 removes the earlier '100 views' labels while revising runtimes, without specifying replacement scan counts or explaining measurement conditions; whether the in-the-wild evaluation settings changed is unresolved.

E4.justification: The training-data and attention-prior ablations, diffusion-refinement illustrations, and real-world robustness case studies are retained. Figure 7 uses the same registered scene outputs and introduces no new robustness condition or diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Repeated-run information, seeds, uncertainty reporting, and statistical estimation practices are unchanged. Figure 7's revised runtimes and added memory measurements are point estimates without uncertainty information.

E6.justification: Figure 7 replaces approximately 0.38 s for each scene with 0.547 s for the kitchen/living room and 0.471 s for the study room, and adds GPU-memory values of 3.1 GB and 3.0 GB respectively. Tables 1–5 and the qualitative registration outputs are unchanged. Unspecified timing conditions prevent interpreting this as a demonstrated same-setting slowdown.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, and prior-aware variational lower-bound derivation in Appendix B are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about feed-forward multiview registration, transferred attention priors, diffusion refinement, accuracy, and efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of attention transfer, training-data scaling, refinement, and real-world robustness are unchanged. No explanation or qualification accompanies Figure 7's revised resource measurements.

D1.justification: Figure 7 adds scene-specific GPU-memory information but removes the explicit 100-view counts, reducing documentation of the corresponding input sizes. Implementation settings, hardware descriptions, encoder details, and code-access information elsewhere are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, bibliography, citations, and positioning relative to pairwise registration and synchronization methods are identical.

P1.justification: The arXiv version/date stamp changes, and Figure 7's scene headings are locally reformatted and reworded. The paper's prose, section ordering, and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 7 changes from side-by-side scene panels to larger vertically stacked panels, with additional input thumbnails, revised arrows and colors, and runtime/memory annotations. Its caption and registered outputs are retained; all other figures and tables are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The enlarged Figure 7 improves readability and adds useful per-scene memory information. However, removing the 100-view labels weakens interpretation and reproducibility of its revised resource measurements, whose changed timing conditions are unexplained. With the rest of the paper unchanged, these opposing local effects do not establish a reliable net quality improvement or deterioration.
